goal: You are a developer starting a small project that has no OAW files yet. Use oaw.py init to add the default tools, repeat init, and inspect the installation with doctor and skills.
notes: Offline standard-library commands. Uses only this folder for configuration, cache and temporary files; no host agent is launched.

goal: You maintain a project with an existing knowledge index and want OAW's knowledge and improvement tools. Install them with oaw.py init --profile knowledge --with-improve, then inspect the project with doctor.
setup:
/usr/bin/python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
files = {'project/docs/knowledge/index.md': '# Team knowledge\n\nRelease notes live here.\n'}
for name, content in files.items():
    path = Path(name)
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(content, encoding='utf-8')
PY
notes: Offline standard-library commands. Uses only this folder for configuration, cache and temporary files; no host agent is launched.

goal: You are returning to a project and want to read its saved observations in small portions. The project has OAW and three dated memory entries; use context_hub.py memory recall with a limit and continue with the returned cursor, then read the text form.
setup:
/usr/bin/python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
files = {'project/.agents/memory.md': '# Memory

---

## [2026-10-28] [NOTE] needle first
First project observation.

## [2026-10-27] [NOTE] needle second
Second project observation.

## [2026-10-26] [NOTE] needle third
Third project observation.
'}
for name, content in files.items():
    path = Path(name)
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(content, encoding='utf-8')
PY
commands: (cd project && /usr/bin/python3 scripts/context_hub.py memory recall needle --limit 1 --max-chars 900 --json) > recall-first.json

cursor="$(/usr/bin/python3 -c 'import json; print(json.load(open("recall-first.json"))["continuation"])')"
(cd project && /usr/bin/python3 scripts/context_hub.py memory recall needle --limit 1 --max-chars 900 --cursor "$cursor" --json)
notes: Continuation is obtained from the preceding JSON result, never hard-coded. Keep the memory files and recall options unchanged between these commands.

goal: You have been using a cached code index and have just added another function to a project module. Use code_index.py stats and find --frozen to inspect the saved index, then run find and stats normally and repeat the query.
setup:
/usr/bin/python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p = Path('project/pkg/util.py')
p.write_text(p.read_text(encoding='utf-8') + '\n\ndef freshly_added_wombat():\n    pass\n', encoding='utf-8')
PY
notes: Setup intentionally creates a cache before adding a function. Frozen commands may print cache-state information on stderr while returning 0. The explicit cache directory stays inside the working folder.
